chunks.subject: AP European History
chunks.title: LEQ — Long Essay Question (6 points) — Q3 Set 1: Differences in the Arts, 1750 to 1950
chunks.content: AP European History LEQ, 6 points, standardized rubric. A Thesis/Claim [1]. B Contextualization [1]. C Evidence [0–2]: (1) two specific relevant pieces; (1) evidence used to support the argument. D Analysis and Reasoning [0–2]: (1) reasoning process (comparison/continuity-and-change) framing the argument; (1) complex understanding. Q3 Set 1 prompt: evaluate the extent of differences in the arts in Europe in the period 1750 to 1950. Common failure: no defensible thesis; reasoning present without complexity; evidence not tied to the argument.

chunks.content: Q3 (Set 1) scored 6/6 (Thesis 1, Context 1, Evidence 2, Analysis 2). Full credit across thesis, contextualization, used evidence, reasoning process, and complex understanding. Full-credit model.

chunks.title: LEQ Q3 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 3B, 4/6
chunks.content: Q3 (Set 1) scored 4/6 (Thesis 0, Context 1, Evidence 2, Analysis 1). Earned contextualization, both Evidence points, and one Analysis point (reasoning process). Lost the Thesis and the Complexity point. Illustrates the frequent 'strong evidence, no scorable thesis' 4-point profile.

chunks.title: LEQ Q3 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 3C, 2/6
chunks.content: Q3 (Set 1) scored 2/6 (Thesis 0, Context 1, Evidence 0, Analysis 1). Earned only contextualization and one Analysis point (attempted a reasoning process). Lost the Thesis and both Evidence points (no specific, used evidence). Illustrates a low LEQ with context and framing but no argument thesis or substantiating evidence.
